To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) intrinsic motivation predicts performance, (b) incentives predict performance, (c) incentives and intrinsic motivation predict performance jointly, (d) incentives and intrinsic motivate predict performance differently, and (e) the relationship between intrinsic motivation and performance is moderated by the contingency between incentives and performance.

(a) intrinsic motivation is an important predictor of performance, and (b) incentives are an important predictor of the quantity of performance, whereas intrinsic motivation is more important to quality of performance.

intrinsic motivation and extrinsic incentive are positively associated with performance, and the association between intrinsic motivation and performance is stronger when extrinsic incentives are less salient to performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation interact to influence performance.
the effects of extrinsic incentives on intrinsic motivation.
the interrelationship among extrinsic incentives, intrinsic motivation, and performance, and how this interrelationship is moderated by incentive salience and performance type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

intrinsic motivation and extrinsic motivation are not necessarily in conflict, but rather that they are complementary, and that both can predict and explain a substantial amount of variance in task performance.
intrinsic motivation and extrinsic rewards are not mutually exclusive, but are complementary.
intrinsic motivation is important for performance, but incentives also matter.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relationship between motivation and performance is not as simple and straightforward as many people assume.
intrinsic motivation is an important factor in performance, but the relationship is not straightforward and depends on how incentives are structured.
intrinsic motivation is an important predictor of performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the provision of incentives is not necessarily detrimental to performance and that incentives and intrinsic motivation can be complementary.
the provision of incentives does not necessarily undermine intrinsic motivation.
intrinsic motivation and extrinsic incentive are not necessarily at odds with each other, and they both predict performance, but in different ways.
